doc.title: Marty Grosz interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995

title: Favorite musicians to play with abroad
summary: He mentions Ralph Sutton, Davern and Wilber of the Summit Reunion, and bassist Greg Cohen.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Who—when you are able to play with different people overseas, who are some of your favorite musicians to play with? Is that, that’s probably a big question? Are there certain individuals?
No, well like guys from here, but like you mentioned Dick Hyman—

Yeah, I was just over there and played some with Ralph Sutton, he’s a fine player. I also did some things with the Summit Reunion, you know I played with them twenty years ago, Davern and Wilber. They’re fun to play with, did the Bern Jazz Festival, did five concerts, they’re good to play with. I mean a lot of guys are good to play with. I mean if I went through the catalogue, usually of course I try to bring the guys I work with. Like I like Greg. Greg Cohen’s wonderful because he plays acoustic bass. He’s one — New
